issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void on SealSaloon, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (a boolean parameter). This signature mismatch means the solution does not match the specified API and could confuse students or automated graders expecting a no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the specified no-argument method checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon. If internal logging is desired, add an overload or internal helper so that a public no-arg checkOrderReady() exists and delegates to the boolean variant (e.g., public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(true); }). This preserves the solution's logging behavior while matching the problem API.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void on SealSaloon, but the solution implementation defines checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (a different signature). This difference in the method's interface creates a mapping confusion: students reading the specification will implement a no-arg checkOrderReady(), whereas the reference solution expects a boolean parameter. The mismatch increases extraneous cognitive load because the same conceptual operation (attempting to serve ready orders) is represented with different method signatures across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either remove the boolean parameter from the solution's checkOrderReady method (making it checkOrderReady()) and call it without arguments from orderMeal(), or update the problem statement to document the additional boolean parameter and its purpose. Preferably keep the spec's no-arg checkOrderReady() and implement any logging as an internal detail to avoid changing the required API.
